issues.description: Resolver no longer resets req.prepared/needs_more_preparation, leaving an unstated contract break for downstream consumers.
issues.detail: The old resolver loop flipped prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False after the more-prep pass. That contract is gone with no replacement, and any code that checks those flags after resolve() now sees stale state. Either restore the flag reset inside prepare_linked_requirements_more, document the new contract on resolve(), or audit every reader.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more is duplicated verbatim across three command files with no shared seam.
issues.detail: install.py, download.py, and wheel.py each call preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more at the same logical point. The next command that ships (pip lock, hash, etc.) is one forgotten line away from silently regressing #12603. Fold this into a RequirementSet/finalize helper or expose an explicit two-phase API on the resolver.

issues.description: set_dist/_distribution adds a third source of distribution truth with no invariant or invalidation.
issues.detail: get_dist now branches across _distribution, metadata_directory, and local_file_path with no documented precedence. If set_dist is called with a metadata-only dist and the wheel is later unpacked, get_dist keeps returning the stale value. Clear _distribution when metadata_directory/local_file_path changes, or thread the dist as a return value instead of a mutable slot.

issues.description: download_info is synthesized unconditionally in the metadata-only branch with no test pinning its shape.
issues.detail: Setting req.download_info = direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) inside _fetch_metadata_only silently defines what --report and pip lock emit, and assumes source_dir is meaningful for a never-downloaded wheel. The policy belongs to the caller, and the resulting DirectUrl (including hashes) needs a test pinning its exact shape for dry-run and real install.

issues.description: Patch ships zero new tests for the headline dry-run/lock behavior.
issues.detail: The diff claims --dry-run and pip lock no longer fetch full wheels when PEP-658 metadata is available, but the only evidence is a news fragment. A test that runs against an index serving PEP-658 metadata, asserts no wheel bytes were fetched, and pins download_info shape is needed; otherwise the next refactor regresses this silently.

issues.description: set_dist is an undocumented one-line setter with no validation or lifecycle contract.
issues.detail: set_dist mutates authoritative state with no docstring stating when it is legal to call, whether re-setting is allowed, or its relation to metadata_directory. Either make it a property that enforces the lifecycle (set once, metadata-only), assert the precondition, or drop the wrapper and assign the attribute directly at the single call site.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the architectural direction is right: pulling more-preparation out of the resolver so dry-run and pip lock can skip wheel downloads is the correct fix for #12603. But the execution leaks the maintainer cost it was meant to save. The resolver no longer resets prepared/needs_more_preparation, three commands now duplicate the same finalize call with no shared seam, and InstallRequirement gains a third source of distribution truth via set_dist with no invalidation. A fabricated download_info inside the metadata-only branch silently defines what --report and pip lock emit, and the headline behavior ships with no regression test. Needs-work: add the dry-run test, collapse the duplicated call behind one seam, and either restore the flag-reset contract or document and audit it.
